correctness.rationale: Cauchy–Schwarz gives moment log-convexity m_j^2 <= m_{j-1}m_{j+1}, so R_W times the backward coefficient shift is a contraction on the Hilbert coefficient completion. For entire f,g with exterior domination, h=f/g has finitely many poles strictly inside |z|<R_W, is holomorphic at infinity, and hence is rational. Its inverse-variable rational Schur transform H(w)=h(R_W/w) is holomorphic near the closed unit disk. The exact coefficient identity Q(R_W B)f=P(R_W B)g yields f=H(R_W B)g; the standard rational von Neumann inequality proves the full infinite-dimensional comparison. The constants versus z test proves sharpness for every larger radius. CHECK.py passed exact-rational polynomial and moment checks; these are illustrative, not a substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly leaves large-Gamma and sharply ring-concentrated radial weights unresolved and proves its sufficient measure criterion can fail for such weights. The new theorem completely settles both families, and indeed every measurable radial Hilbert weight with finite moments, at the exact optimal radius. The underlying shift-contraction/rational-Schur mechanism is reusable structural mathematics, not a numerically modest parameter improvement or textbook restatement.
